attributes.desc: How long it takes: xs 15m, sm 30m, md 1h, lg 2h, xl 3h, 2xl–5xl 5–20h for a task (projects: xs 2h … ultimate 2,500h). Unsized tasks count as md. Weighs progress and XP (10 XP = 1 hour); Neovim shows what a size is worth at the end of the line as you type it.
Due date: the reviews list it as due or overdue, and the planner ranks it higher as it nears.
Priority, 1 the highest: ranks work in the planner and the projects picker. XP is unchanged unless xp.modifiers says otherwise.
Importance, 1 the highest: ranks work like @p.
The area it serves: 4.1 is [A/#4.1], 1.2/Fitness the label Fitness under 1.2. Its XP counts for that area (area XP). Work with none earns for @a(0.1) until the daily review gives it one.
The project a line belongs to (1.4 is [P/#1.4]): m in the daily review, or Move on the web review, puts it there and drops the attribute.
When it was finished (added when you tick it). Dates its XP; on a project or objective heading it marks the whole thing done.
A task's id, added for you: lines with the same @id in the calendar and a project are one task (a copy).

A reference: author and year. Tag searches find it by either, @[*/author(smith)], @[*/year(2020)], or whole, @[*/ref(Smith, 2020)]; cite it in the text with a footnote, [^Smith, 2020], defined on a line of its own: [^Smith, 2020]: the full citation.
Its XP outright, instead of what its @size or tasks add up to.
Parked on purpose: not listed as stale or unscheduled (z in the weekly review toggles it).
How long it takes: a calendar entry's length, a task's minutes in the planner's capacity.
Time worked on it, added by the web app's clocks. Shown in the reviews; it doesn't pay XP.
The line's time, as 14:00 at the start of the line does (@from(14:00) @to(15:30) for a range).

Notify minutes before (several allowed), at the end of a range, at a time of day, or a day before; @notify alone on an untimed line notifies on the day at 09:00; no silences it. Timed lines notify at their time anyway.
Something you plan around (an appointment, a flight): listed under Coming up and marked on the web's month grid.
Published in the server's /calendar.ics for other calendars to subscribe to.
A timed line that doesn't take your time: the planner's capacity doesn't count it as busy.
How often the entry shows: daily, weekly, monthly, yearly, or every n days/weeks/months/years (2d, 3w, 6m, 2y, counted from @from).
Which days a repeating entry lands on; alone it repeats on those days.
A range: the first and last day (both included), or a time range on the line.
A birthday: a year shows the age after the entry's text; a day repeats it every year on that day.
A repeating task's copy done on another day: the day it stands for (added for you).
The section starts folded in Neovim each time the note is shown.
The heading level that starts a slide when the note is shown as slides.
Slides: reveal this line (or each item of the slide) one click at a time.
A tag search finds attributes by their value too: key(value), compared without case or extra spaces.
Any other bare @word is a tag, found by tag searches (@[rust]). In a note's header it tags the note.
